Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) occupational therapy practice management software vendors (WebPT for rehab therapy at $79-$329/month, Fusion Web Clinic for OT/speech practices, TherapyNotes for multidisciplinary behavioral health including OT, Raintree Systems for rehab therapy, HENO for outpatient OT, ClinicSource, Prompt EMR) selling integrated platforms for scheduling, clinical documentation, treatment plans, billing, insurance claims, and outcomes tracking at $79-$329/month per clinician ($948-$3,948/year LTV) — software vendors routinely pay $5,000-$12,000/year for OT marketing lists to acquire customers, making a $149 CSV deliver 33×-80× cost savings; (2) continuing education (CEU) providers selling mandatory state-required professional development hours — all 50 states require OTs to complete 12-36 CEU hours biennially for license renewal (AOTA/NBCOT require 36 hours triennially for OTR certification maintenance; specific state requirements vary: California requires 24 hours biennially, Texas requires 24 hours biennially, Florida requires 24 hours biennially, New York requires 36 hours triennially), creating mandatory recurring $200-$700/year spend per OT on accredited CEU courses from vendors like MedBridge, AOTA Online Learning, OccupationalTherapy.com, PDResources, and university-based CE programs; (3) healthcare recruiters and clinical staffing agencies placing OTs in schools (13% of OTs work in school-based settings per AOTA), hospitals, outpatient clinics, skilled nursing facilities, home health agencies, pediatric clinics, hand therapy centers, and private practices — recruiters charge 15-25% of first-year salary for permanent placements, generating $14,000-$28,000 in fees per OT hire at typical $70K-$110K salary levels (BLS median $93,180 as of May 2023, with pediatric OTs at $70K-$95K, hand therapy specialists at $85K-$120K, hospital-based OTs at $80K-$105K, SNF-based OTs at $85K-$115K); and (4) medical suppliers and durable medical equipment (DME) vendors marketing occupational therapy assessment tools (Peabody Developmental Motor Scales PDMS-2, Beery VMI Visual-Motor Integration test, sensory processing assessments, ADL assessment kits), therapy equipment and supplies (weighted vests, sensory integration equipment, therapy balls, fine motor tools, adaptive equipment, hand therapy putty and tools, pediatric therapy toys, wheelchair seating and positioning aids), electronic health record systems, and professional resources. All 50 states require professional license to practice occupational therapy, with state-specific Boards of Occupational Therapy or Departments of Professional Regulation maintaining public searchable license verification databases. National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT) offers voluntary national OTR (Occupational Therapist Registered) and COTA (Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant) certification with online verification system — while NBCOT certification is voluntary at national level, most states require NBCOT exam passage as prerequisite for initial state licensure, making NBCOT a valuable supplementary validation source. Key fields per license: OT full name, state license number, license status (active, inactive, expired, disciplined), license type (OT vs. OTA occupational therapy assistant), initial licensure date, expiration/renewal date, NBCOT certification status (where applicable), practice address (where disclosed), and disciplinary history. Zero PII — all professional licensing data under state occupational therapy practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 50+ state occupational therapy licensing boards (formats vary by state — each maintains separate online verification system), deduplicate multi-state licensees (many OTs hold licenses in multiple states for travel therapy), integrate NBCOT verification data as supplementary credential marker, normalize license status and type categories, and flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or per-contact pricing ($0.15-$0.50 per contact which scales to $15,000-$50,000 for 100K contacts), not one-time CSV downloads. Audience size is substantial: approximately 148,000 licensed occupational therapists nationwide (BLS reports 148,940 OTs employed as of May 2023), plus NBCOT reports approximately 140,000+ active OTR certifications (excludes COTAs and inactive certifications), creating a TAM of 3,000+ potential B2B buyers across practice management software, CEU providers, recruiters, and medical/DME suppliers. Score is 8 due to strong validated willingness-to-pay from 7+ commercial vendors at premium pricing (BizProspex $340, ContactOut 119K+ contacts updated March 2026, DataCaptive 52K+ OTs, Dietrich Direct $69 baseline), confirmed public data availability across all 50 state licensing boards plus NBCOT verification, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives creating 33×-80× cost advantage, substantial professional population (148K OTs), mandatory CEU requirements driving recurring B2B buyer demand, and four distinct high-LTV B2B buyer segments with proven purchasing behavior in rehab therapy software, continuing education, recruiting, and DME markets — comparable strength to SLP opportunity with similar TAM size, buyer segments, and commercial validation.

data_wanted: All 50 states require professional license to practice occupational therapy, with state-specific Boards of Occupational Therapy, Departments of Professional Regulation, or combined health professions boards maintaining public searchable license verification databases. National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy (NBCOT at nbcot.org) provides certification verification system for OTR (Occupational Therapist Registered) and COTA (Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant) credentials — while NBCOT certification is voluntary at national level, most states require NBCOT exam passage as prerequisite for initial state licensure, making NBCOT a valuable supplementary data source for credential validation and certification status. State occupational therapy boards provide online license lookup systems (formats vary significantly by state — some offer downloadable rosters, most require individual web-based lookups or scraping). Key fields per license: OT full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 6-12 characters), initial licensure date (date of first OT license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date (most states use biennial renewal cycles with 12-36 CEU hour requirements depending on state), license status (active, inactive, expired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), license type or credential level (OT/OTR for occupational therapist vs. OTA/COTA for occupational therapy assistant — IMPORTANT: scope to OT/OTR only, exclude assistants as they have different buyer markets and practice scope), NBCOT certification status (certified OTR or not certified — cross-reference with NBCOT online verification system), NBCOT certification number (where applicable), specialty certifications (Certified Hand Therapist CHT, Board Certified in Pediatrics BCP, Certified Brain Injury Specialist CBIS — where disclosed by state), practice setting or employer (hospital, school, SNF, outpatient clinic, home health, private practice — where voluntarily disclosed or required by state), practice address (where publicly disclosed), education credentials (master's or doctoral degree in occupational therapy, university — where listed), and disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, consent orders, license restrictions — private warnings not included). Target all active and inactive (but not permanently revoked) OT/OTR licenses only — EXCLUDE occupational therapy assistants (OTA/COTA) as they are distinct credential with different buyer segments, salary levels ($61,730 median for OTAs vs. $93,180 for OTs per BLS), and scope of practice (assistants work under OT supervision, cannot evaluate patients independently, less attractive to software vendors and recruiters). Approximately 148,000 licensed occupational therapists nationwide (BLS reports 148,940 OTs employed as of May 2023; NBCOT reports 140,000+ active OTR certifications as of 2023 excluding assistants and inactive certifications). Target output: 150K rows, one per license (some OTs hold licenses in multiple states for travel therapy or cross-border practice). Data is 100% public per state occupational therapy practice acts and state Freedom of Information laws — OT licensing and disciplinary records are public information under state professional regulation statutes.
